title: Annotatio III §.VIII: After Cassel — Frederick William the Great’s many peace attempts hindered by Dannhauer’s circle
pass_a_gloss: But after the Cassel [colloquy], the very many pacific attempts of FREDERICK WILLIAM THE GREAT, Elector of Brandenburg — called by our Author p. 341, by his excellent desert, that Mars of Germany and Upholder of Liberty as well as Religion — are even known to the public, yet were likewise hindered by other Theologians in the neighborhood of the March, either Disciples or Symmystae of that Dannhauer, for the deadly hatred with which they were stirred against the Reformed, and they all but blasphemously prayed God that He would fill them more and more with hatred of the Calvinists (truly not knowing what they asked).
pass_b_english: After Cassel, the many peace attempts of Frederick William the Great, Elector of Brandenburg — whom our Author (p. 341) rightly calls Germany’s Mars and upholder of liberty and religion — are even publicly known;
yet other theologians near the March, Dannhauer’s disciples or fellow-initiates, blocked them out of deadly hatred of the Reformed,
and all but blasphemously prayed God to fill them ever more with hatred of Calvinists — not knowing what they asked.
source_text: Post Cassellanum verò, Mavortis istius Germaniae, Libertatisque juxtà ac Religionis Statoris, optimô suô meritô, Autori nostro p. 341. dicti, FRIDERICI WILHELMI MAGNI Electoris Brandenburgici, pacifica conamina quam plurima, vel in vulgus nota sunt, similiter tamen à Theologis aliis, in vicinia Marchiae, Danhaueri istius vel Discipulis, vel Symmystis, pro exitiali, quô adversus Reformatos odio perciti erant, & Deum tantùm non blasphemè precabantur, quò se magis magisque odio Calvinianorum impleret, (nescientes profectò quid peterent,) praepedita.
notes: Frederick William Great / Dannhauer circle; Autor p. 341.
